title: The platform at rest: cluster, node pools, queues, verifiers and stores
purpose: Show what was built before anything runs: a standard EKS cluster (not Auto Mode) with a CPU pool and a GPU pool on a pinned accelerated AMI, Kueue and JobSet, the two queues, the sandboxed verifier pool, the health monitor, and the four stores in S3.

checks.description: the cluster is ACTIVE on Kubernetes 1.37, and EKS Auto Mode is not enabled
checks.because: Terraform created a standard EKS cluster: no compute_config block, so EKS does not manage the nodes.

checks.description: the GPU pool is an EKS managed node group on the NVIDIA AMI, at the pinned release, with a GPU taint
checks.because: The release version is a Terraform variable, so the NVIDIA driver and CUDA user space change only when the file changes.

checks.description: two GPU nodes are Ready and each advertises one GPU
checks.because: The NVIDIA device plugin, installed by Terraform on the GPU pool only, advertises nvidia.com/gpu on each node.

checks.description: the GPU nodes are ordinary EC2 instances the account can see (and count, and prove gone)
checks.because: Managed node group instances are listed by EC2, unlike Auto Mode's managed instances.

checks.description: Kueue 0.20.7, JobSet 0.13.1 and the NVIDIA device plugin 0.20.2 are running, with the verifier pool and the health monitor
checks.because: Each controller is a Helm release pinned in Terraform; the image tags are the evidence of the versions.

checks.description: production owns both GPUs and reclaims them; ablation owns none and may only borrow
checks.because: Two ClusterQueues in one cohort. The ablation queue has no quota of its own, so everything it runs is borrowed and can be reclaimed.

checks.description: the verifier namespace denies all egress and enforces the restricted Pod Security level
checks.because: A NetworkPolicy with an empty egress list, enforced by the VPC CNI's network policy agent (enabled in the add-on's configuration).

checks.description: four workload identities: trainer, datagen, evaluator, health-monitor (and none for the verifiers)
checks.because: EKS Pod Identity associations, each with a role scoped to the S3 prefixes it needs.

checks.description: twelve versioned datasets are in the store, each with a content hash
checks.because: Generated by datasets/make_datasets.py from a fixed seed and uploaded by Terraform.
